title: Exact closed operations and normalized evaluation for strict systems
statement: Let i:Z↪T be a closed immersion of schemes, and U an object of T_proet whose structure map is the complementary quasi-compact open immersion [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For every inverse sequence B of commutative ring sheaves, ClosedData(i,B) [def-sp-semilinear-open-closed-data] is inhabited. Thus this assertion concerns only exact closed pull/push and their normalized ordinary level comparisons: it contains no open operation, localization exact sequence, complexes or coefficient-change comparison.

source.place: Tags 09A5, 03D6 and 09BM; parent steps 1, 2, 4 and the exactness part of step 5

proof.text: At each n, direct image is restriction to base-change objects with the ring unit action. Comparing both constructions gives identity additive section maps. Naturality of the ring unit identifies their module actions and horizontal restrictions, yielding pushEvaluation with its section normalization.

The sheafification defining inverse image uses only vertical covers at a fixed index. Transpose the preceding section comparison along the actual module adjunctions; the result is an invertible pullEvaluation comparison and its defining mate equation is unitEvaluation. Uniqueness of left adjoints compares the level pullback with the small-model inverse image.

Kernels and cokernels of systems are computed at every index: exact scalar restriction induces their transitions, and uniqueness of kernel/cokernel factorizations proves the system laws and universal properties. Finite biproducts are componentwise. Apply immersion inverse-image exactness and closed direct-image exactness at each level (the complement is quasi-compact), and transport with the normalized comparisons. This proves additivity and both finite preservation claims.
